knowledge_point.title: Using Column Operations to Create a Row of Zeros in a 4x4 Matrix

question.:question/problem:
$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}3 & 1 & 0 & 5 \\ -3 & 6 & 3 & -6 \\ 3 & -4 & 6 & 0 \\ -3 & 3 & 9 & -8\end{bmatrix},\,B=\begin{bmatrix}3 & 7 & 3 & -1 \\ -3 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & 2 & 9 & -6 \\ -3 & -3 & 6 & -2\end{bmatrix}
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $B$ above. By applying three matrix elementary column operations

- $C_{2}:=\ldots$
- $C_{3}:=\ldots$
- $C_{4}:=C_{4}-2C_{1}$

each of the form $C_i:=C_i+kC_{1},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the missing elementary column operations?

knowledge_point.title: Using Column Operations to Create a Row of Zeros in a 4x4 Matrix

question.:question/problem:
$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}-6 & 3 & -9 & -15 \\ -4 & -6 & 5 & 3 \\ 6 & 9 & 3 & 6 \\ 7 & 6 & 3 & 1\end{bmatrix},\,B=\begin{bmatrix}0 & 3 & 0 & 0 \\ -16 & -6 & -13 & -27 \\ 24 & 9 & 30 & 51 \\ 19 & 6 & 21 & 31\end{bmatrix}
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $B$ above. By applying three matrix elementary column operations

- $C_{1}:=\ldots$
- $C_{3}:=\ldots$
- $C_{4}:=C_{4}+5C_{2}$

each of the form $C_i:=C_i+kC_{2},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the missing elementary column operations?
